question: Can each bot's role be written down once — name, role, the tools it may use and under what condition, what it must never do, and what it owns — so that a machine, not a reader's goodwill, says whether a bot was allowed to do a thing, and every 'never' in Simon's roster holds?
why: Simon's bot-team spec (2026-11-01). §8 step 2: PERSONA FILES. §1: each persona has a name, a role, allowed tools, forbidden actions and the outputs it owns. §0: tools are fenced per bot. §6: the builder is never the auditor; the auditor runs on a different model and config from the builders.

design.roster: data/roster.json (this public repo; it names no private repo): a vocabulary of tools, each with a class — read, write (inside the company), gated (needs the auditor's PASS) or outward (leaves the company: needs Simon's go) — and the eight personas, each { id, name, role, runs_on, runtime { model, config }, tools: [id | { tool, when: ['auditor-pass' | 'simon-go', …] }], forbidden: [id], content: [rule], owns: [output] }.
design.kernel: src/roster.mjs: problems(roster) lists what is wrong with a roster; may(roster, persona, tool, { auditorPass, simonGo }) → { ok, why } with why one of unknown persona, unknown tool, forbidden, off-list, needs the auditor's PASS, needs Simon's go; an outward tool needs Simon's go whatever the roster says. toolOf(line) names the tool a feed line used (a post line by reach is post.draft; a decision line with verdict approve is decision.approve; a pause is pause.write; and so on), so the auditor can fence what bots wrote as well as what they called.
design.cards: One card per persona in the team's private shared repo (team/<id>.md), generated by tools/team-cards.mjs from the roster and stamped with the roster's SHA-256; a card is never edited by hand. The cards for bots on Grok Bot's computer carry how to write the feed from there.

clauses.spec: Never merges to main without an auditor PASS and Simon's go
Never releases without an auditor PASS and Simon's go
Read-only watching; logs leads and gaps
clauses.rule: every tool scout may use is class read, or feed.write, lead.log or gap.log

clauses.spec: Never signs anything the auditor hasn't passed
Runs on a different model and config from the builders
clauses.rule: the auditor's runtime model and config each differ from builder's and from kar's

claims.claim: The roster is whole: the eight §1 personas, exactly the feed's persona ids, each with a name, a role, where it runs, a runtime, at least one tool, at least one forbidden action and at least one owned output; problems(roster) is empty.

Every 'never' holds as a machine answer: for each of the 21 sealed clauses, may() refuses every named tool without the named condition (forbidden outright: refused even with an auditor PASS and Simon's go), allows it once the condition is met where a condition is named, the content rules are on the persona, scout's tools are all read or logging, and the auditor's runtime differs from the builders'.
The fence: for every persona and every outward tool, may() refuses it without Simon's go — even with an auditor PASS — and no persona may write an auditor verdict except the auditor.
claims.pass: every pair refused; verdict.write only on the auditor

claims.claim: One role, one owner: no output is owned by two personas, and every feed kind a persona may write maps to a tool it is allowed.
claims.pass: no output owned twice; every persona can write the kinds its role needs (task/note/blocker at least), with no off-list tool

claims.claim: Total: 3,000 fuzzed calls to may(), toolOf() and problems() (garbage rosters, personas, tools, contexts, lines) never throw; may() never says yes to an unknown persona or tool.
The cards are the roster: each persona's card is regenerated from the roster byte for byte and carries the roster's SHA-256; a changed roster makes every card's stamp stale.
claims.pass: 8 of 8 regenerate identical; a one-byte roster change makes 8 of 8 stale

scope: Step 2 writes the roles down and makes the fence a function. It does not yet watch the bots: comparing what each bot actually did against the fence is the auditor's job (step 3). Grok Bot's three roles run on Grok Bot's own computer; their cards tell them how to stay inside the fence, and the auditor checks what they write.
kept: Every result is kept as measured, held or failed.
